# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `units_present` against input/, which is EMPTY apart from a .gitkeep placeholder. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/units_present/expect.json for the _env caveat and for why a `pass` fixture for
# this check cannot be written at all.
#
# THIS CASE: NEITHER UNIT FILE EXISTS -- the state of a machine that has never run `fmonero setup
# --units`, which is the state of THIS machine today (DESIGN.md §1.1: no Monero binaries, no units).
# status `warn`, the same as the drifted case, because §7.1 gives the row ONE severity and one fixer:
# rewrite them from units::render_*. "Absent" and "drifted" have the same remedy, so they are not
# separate statuses -- but THE DETAIL MUST DISTINGUISH THEM, because the user-facing meaning differs
# completely: absent means "run setup", drifted means "something changed these".
# THIS CASE IS WHAT CATCHES A DETECTOR THAT READS A FILE AND UNWRAPS THE ERROR. The natural shape --
# read both files, compare to the rendered bytes -- panics or returns Err on a missing file, and the
# doctor's contract is that every detector is a pure fn detect(&Probes) -> Verdict over one run's probes
# (§7): the I/O belongs in probes.rs and a missing file must arrive as data, not as a failure. Without
# this case the check works on every machine that HAS units and dies on the machine that most needs the
# advice.
# `fixable` TRUE, class B, same Action as the drifted case: WriteFile{unit path, units::render_*(ctx),
# 0o644} then RunArgv{["systemctl","--user","daemon-reload"], inverse: the same} (§7.1). For an ABSENT
# file the `before` sha256 recorded in actions.jsonl has nothing to hash, and `doctor undo` must then
# REMOVE the file it created rather than restore bytes -- a case §7's WriteFile inverse should state
# explicitly, and one the Phase 2 doctor agent must decide and record.
# ON THIS MACHINE TODAY the real `doctor` run reaches this check with real verdicts (the `units` group is
# not skipped by monerod_installed -- §4b's GREEN row skips only node/wallet/storage), so this fixture's
# answer and the live answer should agree. That makes it the one units_present case that is checkable
# twice.
#
# X37 (2026-09-19): the two expectations were the two UNIT FILE NAMES, which §2o.2 says a systemd
# user unit is never given in prose — the detail read `fmonero-monerod.service has not been written
# yet. fmonero-wallet-rpc.service has not been written yet.` The subjects are now *your node* and
# *the wallet service*, as every other row in this group already says, and the file names are in
# `doctor --json` and under the settings keys that hold them. The two cases still have to read
# DIFFERENTLY — absent means "run setup", drifted means "something changed these" — and these two
# expectations are what holds that apart.
detail_contains: Your node has not been set up yet.
The wallet service has not been set up yet.
